text:
Lina: filing INC-7892 — customer reports function/toolcall failing in JSON mode. They say some optional fields that have defaults in the function schema are getting stripped and causing a 422 schema validation. Paste from their error below.

Lina: customer error (copied):
```
HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "error": "function_call_validation_failed",
  "details": [{
    "path": ["items"],
    "message": "field required"
  }]
}
```

Lina: function definition they gave (simplified):
```json
{
  "name": "create_order",
  "args_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "order_id": {"type":"string"},
      "items": {"type":"array", "items": {"type":"object"}, "default": []},
      "metadata": {"type":"object", "default": {}}
    },
    "required": ["order_id"]
  }
}
```

Sam: thanks Lina. Do we have the raw request the customer sent? cc @Ingrid for JSON mode implications.

Lina: pasted the curl they showed in their ticket (they claim they didn't include items or metadata, expecting defaults):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"fn":"create_order","args":{"order_id":"ORD-12345"},"mode":"json"}'
```

Ingrid: repro attempt on staging (ran same curl). I see the validation error Lina pasted. Attaching the service-side log snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T10:02:13Z] request_id=abc123 validator: missing required property "items" at /args
stack: ValidationError: items is required
    at validate (/srv/runtime/validators.js:78:15)
    at processFnCall (/srv/runtime/handler.js:342:9)
```

Ingrid: interestingly, the runtime schema step checks for presence of properties and treats omitted properties with "default" as optional, but we're getting a strict required check. Suspect something upstream stripped the default metadata before validation.

Sam: did anything change around proxy or the request canonicalization layer recently? I remember a proxy upgrade last week.

Raj: yes — proxy v2.3.0 rolled last Wed. There was a change to drop keys with null/empty defaults in an attempt to compress traffic (ticket PROXY-412). Could be related.

eng-oncall: can we confirm whether the request arriving at the runtime still contains the function schema defaults? Ingrid — can you dump the raw request body the runtime receives (before any canonicalization)?

Ingrid: grabbed raw HTTP body from ingress logs: it is exactly what the customer sent (no items/metadata). The defaults live in the function schema, not the request. But we also rely on an intermediary to merge defaults into the args for some legacy handlers. Looks like that merge step is a separate service (arg-merger) behind the proxy. Checking arg-merger logs now.

Ingrid: arg-merger logs show: when request passes through proxy v2.3.0 it sends an abbreviated payload header `X-Payload-Strip: true` and arg-merger returns early without injecting defaults. Example arg-merger trace: 
```
[2026-02-12T10:02:14Z] arg-merger request_id=abc123 mode=json received strip=true -> skipping defaults injection
```

Lina: so arg-merger used to ignore that header and always injected defaults. New proxy set it and arg-merger honors it. That explains why defaults never reach validator. Customer expecting server to apply default is reasonable.

Sam: severity? Customer had production impact (orders failing). Marking SEV-2 and escalating to platform. cc @Raj

Raj: patch in progress. Quick mitigation: arg-merger can ignore X-Payload-Strip for function/toolcall routes when mode=json, then inject defaults. I'll open a PR and deploy to staging.

eng-oncall: workaround for customers in the meantime: explicitly include the defaults in the payload. e.g.,
```json
{"fn":"create_order","args":{"order_id":"ORD-12345","items":[],"metadata":{}} ,"mode":"json"}
```
Lina: customer accepted workaround and will send a hotfix.

Raj: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/arg-merger/pulls/78 — small guard to skip strip header when fn routes + mode=json. Running CI now, will request a canary deploy.

eng-oncall: after canary and smoke, we should ship a hotfix to prod and then revert proxy's header behavior or update PROXY-412 to be narrower. Also add e2e test that ensures functions with defaulted properties still validate when client omits them.

Sam: adding runbook note for support: if customer sees 422 for omitted defaulted fields, ask for their curl and recommend workaround (explicit defaults) and escalate to platform if many customers affected.

Lina: thanks all — I'll update INC-7892 with repro notes and the workaround. Please ping me when hotfix is live so I can notify the customer. :thumbsup:

support-bot: scheduled incident update posted to INC-7892 — priority SEV-2.
